chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: Buying and pricing corn liquor, burnt-sugar 'red' and needle whiskey
summary: The Italians delivered whiskey by phone; prices, how white was made red, and the effect of needle whiskey.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Where did you get your...your whiskey?

We bought it from the I-talians. If you'd have a automobile...if you had an old Ford--that's all they drove is Fords--and happens if you call the cat who delivers the whiskey. He deliver whiskey all over town to all them plants and after-hours joints and places all over town.
So it was easy to buy?

Yeah, all you do is call up there and tell the man what you want...call the I-talians up and tell 'em what you want...want a half-a-gallon or two gallons, and they bring it right out to your house, and all you hadda do is have your half-pint bottles there, and you pour it up. We had red whiskey and we had white whiskey. You wanted red, cost you thirty-five cents more. You take burnt sugar and cook it on the stove, and pour it into the white whiskey and make it red, and that costs fifteen cents more. Costs twenty-five cents for a half-a-pint.
Twenty-five cents for a half-pint of corn liquor, and thirty-five cents you got your red and white...it was red.
And your red was burnt sugar.
Your red was burnt sugar...what it is when you mix it up...lessen you bought it already red, and then... They had whiskey they called needle whiskey.
It was corn liquor but it had some kind of needle they put down in it, and they mixed somethin' up in it, and you would stir it. You'd stir it till it got red hot, almost boilin'...
You drink a glass o' that, boy, and you really lit up like a church house.
